title: House floor vote on H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act — data centers pay the full cost of grid upgrades
source: NEWS: RE-DATED 09-17 -> 09-15 by this event's own initial research, on three House sources fetched direct 2026-09-15 that all name Tuesday. (1) The Majority Leader's DAILY schedule (majorityleader.gov/schedule) has exactly one current entry, 'TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 15 — On Tuesday, the House will meet at 10:00 a.m. for morning hour and noon legislative business. First votes expected: 1:30 p.m. Last votes expected: 5:00 p.m.', and lists 'H.R. 9340 - Ratepayer Protection Act, as amended (Sponsored by Rep. Evans (CO) / Energy and Commerce Committee)' under that day's 'Legislation Considered Under Suspension of the Rules'. (2) repcloakroom.house.gov lists H.R. 9340 under Tuesday, September 15 (and under Monday 09-14, whose votes were postponed to 6:30 p.m.). (3) docs.house.gov/floor still carries it as 'Added 09/10/2026 at 08:30 PM' with its text under /billsthisweek/20260914/. The Clerk's own record (clerk.house.gov/evs/2026, fetched 2026-09-15) shows the latest roll call is No. 297 at 2026-09-14 19:16 and H.R. 9340 is not among the 297 taken, so the vote was still pending at that timestamp. The prior 09-17 date was DERIVED by the midterm-elections sweep of 2026-09-15 as 'the last scheduled legislative day of the calendared week' before the daily schedule published; it is superseded, not defended. Stays estimate: a suspension item is 'legislation considered', a postponement to a later day of the same week is routine (this very schedule carries a 'Postponed Suspensions' block), and this calendar has no confirmed-class source prefix for a House floor calendar (CONFIRMED_PREFIX is IR/CAL/BLS/FED/PJM/SEC and CAL: is used zero times here). The id keeps its 09-17 slug because the id is the file name and the research branch key. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: Initial research 2026-09-15: three independent legs all land on stand-aside, and none of them is 'it is too small to bother with'. (1) PASSAGE IS NEAR-CERTAIN AND NEAR-CERTAINLY INERT — suspension votes in the 119th Congress 2nd Session ran 61 of 65 passed (93.8%; 96.8% excluding the two proposed constitutional amendments), computed from the Clerk's own roll-call index; and the operative text amends PURPA sec. 111(d) to make state regulators CONSIDER a large-load standard for 100MW+ data centers, which Harvard's Ari Peskoe calls 'largely symbolic' with no enforcement mechanism. No appropriation, no cash-flow effect on any tracked name. (2) THE SIGN IS NOT EVEN BEARISH DATA CENTERS — Microsoft and Google back the bill (it supplies political cover as bills rise anyway); the party that objected is the Data Center Coalition, and its objection (Josh Levi, 2026-07-22) is that E&C NARROWED the scope to single out data centers, a scope complaint, not a cost complaint. The naive 'AI backlash, short the AI-energy sleeve' read is backwards. (3) THE TAPE CARRIES NO ATTRIBUTION — equal-weight CEG/VST/NRG/TLN, beta 1.568 to SPY over 251 sessions, daily beta-adjusted excess sd 2.54pp, p90 |excess| 4.00pp; cumulative excess over the four sessions since the bill hit the calendar is -8.17pp = -1.61 sigma. The one day that clears the bar (2026-09-14, -5.56pp, 2.19 sigma, past p95) is unattributable: XLU fell -3.48% over the same span though the bill would if anything help regulated utilities, the 10Y went 4.84 -> 5.00 into a bond-proxy sector, and the derating is a year old (TLN -20.6% in a month, CRWV -23.5%). AND THE CORRIDOR SWALLOWS IT: FOMC is 2026-09-16, the morning after. Filed low and kept low. NOT ONE BILL BUT A PACKAGE — H.R. 6633 (High-Capacity Grid Act), H.R. 9332 (Load Forecasting Enhancement Act) and H.R. 9339 (Affordable Innovation for the Grid Act) sit on the same suspension list the same day; deliberately NOT proposed as separate calendar entries (#2946 anti-churn: same day, same vote block, same measured-zero channel) and folded into this entry's scope instead. Senate path is slow: Husted's S. 5028 exists, but Senate ENR has not prioritized data-center energy legislation. Close-out reads the Clerk roll call; if H.R. 9340 is absent from it on 2026-09-16, the bill was postponed or pulled and the entry should be re-dated once more from the Clerk, never rolled forward on a guess. Shadows proposals/house-vote-ratepayer-protection-act-2026-09-17.from-midterm-elections-2026-11-03.json, whose own note instructed exactly this re-dating.
